turn2.differences: The author's five conditions (c1-c5) map directly onto the conditions I identified in step 1: file type, folder location, description content, size threshold, and exact top-level comment count. There is no meaningful gap between the author's list and my own reading of the request.

ambiguity_effects.explain: In principle this could mean 'directly inside' vs 'anywhere within the folder tree,' but Product Specs (8200) has no subfolders in this dataset, so every candidate's folder membership is unambiguous in practice.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: whose description mentions the mobile redesign
ambiguity_effects.explain: Exact-phrase vs. paraphrase readings could matter in general, but no file here sits on that boundary: matching files (8210, 8211, 8213, 8214) explicitly say 'mobile redesign' in their description, while non-matching files (8212, 8217, 8220, 8215) don't reference it at all in the description (8212's mention is only in a tag, a different field), so neither reading changes any outcome.

Decimal (2,000,000 bytes) vs binary (2,097,152 bytes) MB could matter for a borderline file, but the sizes present are either clearly under (1,800,000) or clearly over (2,100,000 and 3,000,000) both thresholds, so the choice of definition never changes which files qualify.

turn2.naturalness_note: The request is plausible as something a real user would ask, but the phrase 'not counting replies' is a level of precision most users wouldn't spontaneously specify when describing comment counts by memory — it reads slightly like a condition added to make the test unambiguous rather than natural phrasing, though it isn't implausible.
